newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares end mixed, ENI, TIM up.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares end mixed, ENI, TIM up.

text.p: Italian shares closed on Wednesday mixed with strong gains by Telecom Italia Mobile and a steady performance by energy group ENI driving the stock index higher in a market dominated by expectations of an interest rate cut.

The all-share Mibtel index finished 0.42 percent higher at 12,372 while the blue chip Mib30 gained 0.6 percent to 18,438. Trading volumes eased slightly to 1,008.7 billion lire from 1,163 billion on Tuesday.
Olivetti shares took a heavy battering, after yesterday's announcement of a capital restructuring and disappointing first quarter performance, closing 6.58 percent lower at 518.1 lire.
Mediobanca and BCI both went into reverse after jointly denying reports of a planned merger between the two banks.

BCI finished 2.84 percent lower at 3,590 lire and Mediobanca was 2.34 percent down at 10,813 lire. Brokers said a joint statement strongly denying the merger reports, which boosted the share price of both banks on Monday and Tuesday, had not completely scotched speculation and some investors continue to believe an alliance cannot be ruled out.

TIM finished 2.75 percent higher at 5,074 lire, while other telecom stocks all retreated. Market watchers believe TIM stands to gain from continued delays by the government in inviting bids for a third mobile phone operating licence.
Ambroveneto surged 2.76 percent among banks closing at 4,099 lire. Generali was almost unchanged at 30,660 lire.
